title.zh: 卷五十八 志第十: 地理一
title.raw: 卷五十八 志第十: 地理一 Volume 58 Treatises 11: Geography 1

sentences.zh: 自封建變為郡縣，有天下者，漢、隋、唐、宋為盛，然幅員之廣，咸不逮元。

translations.literal: Since feudal enfeoffment changed to commanderies and counties, those who held the realm — Han, Sui, Tang, and Song — were at their greatest, yet in territorial extent none matched the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Once the feudal order gave way to commanderies and counties, the dynasties that ruled the realm — Han, Sui, Tang, and Song — each reached their height; yet in sheer territorial breadth, none could compare with the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 漢梗于北狄，隋不能服東夷，唐患在西戎，宋患常在西北。

translations.literal: Han was obstructed by the northern Di, Sui could not subdue the eastern Yi, Tang's troubles lay in the western Rong, and Song's troubles were constantly in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Han was hemmed in by the northern barbarians, Sui failed to bring the eastern tribes to heel, Tang's woes came from the western frontier, and Song's troubles never left the northwest.

sentences.zh: 若元，則起朔漠，併西域，平西夏，滅女真，臣高麗，定南詔，遂下江南，而天下為一，故其地北踰陰山，西極流沙，東盡遼左，南越海表。

translations.literal: As for the Yuan, they rose from the northern deserts, merged the Western Regions, pacified Western Xia, destroyed the Jurchens, made Goryeo submit, settled Nanzhao, then descended on Jiangnan, and the realm became one; thus their territory extended north beyond Yinshan, west to the shifting sands, east to the far reaches of Liaodong, and south beyond the seas.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan, by contrast, rose from the northern steppe, absorbed the Western Regions, pacified Western Xia, destroyed the Jurchen state, brought Goryeo to submission, settled Nanzhao, and finally swept down into Jiangnan until the realm was united. Their domain ran north beyond Yinshan, west to the shifting sands, east to the limits of Liaodong, and south across the seas.

sentences.zh: 蓋漢，東西九千三百二里，南北一萬三千三百六十八里；

translations.literal: The Han realm measured 9,302 li east to west and 13,368 li north to south;
translations.idiomatic: Han territory spanned 9,302 li from east to west and 13,368 li from north to south;

sentences.zh: 唐，東西九千五百一十一里，南北一萬六千九百一十八里；

translations.literal: Tang measured 9,511 li east to west and 16,918 li north to south;
translations.idiomatic: Tang territory measured 9,511 li east to west and 16,918 li north to south;

sentences.zh: 元，東南所至不下漢、唐，而西北則過之，有難以里數限者矣。

translations.literal: The Yuan in the southeast reached no less than Han and Tang, while in the northwest it exceeded them — there were areas that could hardly be bounded by a count in li.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan domain in the southeast was no smaller than Han's or Tang's, while in the northwest it surpassed them both — stretches of land that no tally in li could fully contain.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗六年甲午，滅金，得中原州郡。

translations.literal: Initially, in the sixth year of Taizong (jiayin), Jin was destroyed and the Central Plains commanderies and prefectures were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, in the sixth year of Emperor Taizong (the jiayin year), the Jin dynasty was overthrown and the commanderies and prefectures of the Central Plains came into Mongol hands.

sentences.zh: 七年乙未，下詔籍民，自燕京、順天等三十六路，戶八十七萬三千七百八十一，口四百七十五萬四千九百七十五。

translations.literal: In the seventh year (yiwei), an edict ordered a household registration; from Yanjing, Shuntian, and thirty-six other circuits: 873,781 households and 4,754,975 persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (yiwei), an edict ordered a census of the people. From Yanjing, Shuntian, and thirty-six other circuits there were 873,781 households and 4,754,975 persons.

sentences.zh: 憲宗二年壬子，又籍之，增戶二十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianzong (renzi), another registration was conducted, adding more than 200,000 households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Xianzong (the renzi year), another census was taken, adding more than two hundred thousand households.

sentences.zh: 世祖至元七年，又籍之，又增三十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of the Shizu era (Zhiyuan), another registration was conducted, adding more than 300,000 households.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Zhiyuan era under Emperor Shizu, yet another census was held, adding more than three hundred thousand households.

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Song was pacified and the full territorial map was held.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, the Song was pacified and the dynasty held the complete territorial map.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，又籍之，得戶一千一百八十四萬八百有奇。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, another registration was conducted, yielding 11,840,800-odd households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, another census was taken, yielding a figure of more than eleven million, eight hundred forty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 於是南北之戶總書於策者，一千三百一十九萬六千二百有六，口五千八百八十三萬四千七百一十有一，而山澤溪洞之民不與焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the combined total of north and south households recorded in the registers was 13,196,206, and persons 58,834,711 — not counting the peoples of mountains, marshes, streams, and cave settlements.
translations.idiomatic: The combined north and south total entered in the registers came to 13,196,206 households and 58,834,711 persons — not including the peoples of mountain fastnesses, marshes, stream valleys, and cave settlements.

sentences.zh: 立中書省一，行中書省十有一：曰嶺北，曰遼陽，曰河南，曰陝西，曰四川，曰甘肅，曰雲南，曰江浙，曰江西，曰湖廣，曰征東，分鎮籓服，路一百八十五，府三十三，州三百五十九，軍四，安撫司十五，縣一千一百二十七。

translations.literal: One central Secretariat was established, and eleven Regional Secretariats: Lingbei, Liaoyang, Henan, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Gansu, Yunnan, Jiangzhe, Jiangxi, Huguang, and Zhengdong — dividing governance of the frontier domains. There were 185 circuits, 33 fu, 359 zhou, 4 jun, 15 pacification commissions, and 1,127 counties.
translations.idiomatic: One central Secretariat was established, along with eleven Regional Secretariats — Lingbei, Liaoyang, Henan, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Gansu, Yunnan, Jiangzhe, Jiangxi, Huguang, and Zhengdong — each governing a portion of the frontier domains. The realm comprised 185 circuits, 33 prefectures (fu), 359 subprefectures (zhou), 4 military commands (jun), 15 pacification commissions, and 1,127 counties.

sentences.zh: 文宗至順元年，戶部錢糧戶數一千三百四十萬六百九十九，視前又增二十萬有奇，漢、唐極盛之際，有不及焉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun under Emperor Wenzong, the Ministry of Revenue's registered tax households numbered 13,400,699 — an increase of more than 200,000 over the previous count; at the height of Han and Tang, there were figures that did not reach this.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhishun era under Emperor Wenzong, the Ministry of Revenue counted 13,400,699 tax-paying households — more than two hundred thousand above the earlier figure. Even at the peak of Han and Tang, the numbers had never reached this level.

sentences.zh: 蓋嶺北、遼陽與甘肅、四川、雲南、湖廣之邊，唐所謂羈縻之州，往往在是，今皆賦役之，比於內地；

translations.literal: For the frontiers of Lingbei, Liaoyang, Gansu, Sichuan, Yunnan, and Huguang — where Tang's so-called "loose-rein" prefectures often lay — all are now subject to taxation and corvée, on a par with the interior;
translations.idiomatic: The borderlands of Lingbei, Liaoyang, Gansu, Sichuan, Yunnan, and Huguang — regions where Tang had maintained its loosely governed "tributary" prefectures — now all paid taxes and performed corvée labor on the same terms as the interior;

sentences.zh: 而高麗守東籓，執臣禮惟謹，亦古所未見。

translations.literal: Moreover, Goryeo guarded the eastern frontier and observed the duties of a subject with utmost care — something never before seen in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: while Goryeo held the eastern marches and performed the duties of a vassal with scrupulous fidelity — a state of affairs without precedent in earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 地大民眾，後世狃於治安，而不知詰戎兵、慎封守，積習委靡，一旦有變，而天下遂至於不可為。

translations.literal: The land was vast and the people numerous; later generations grew accustomed to peace and security, not knowing to examine frontier troops or guard the borders carefully. Accumulated habits led to laxity, and once change came, the realm reached a state beyond remedy.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was vast and populous, yet later generations grew complacent in peace, neglecting frontier defense and border vigilance. Habit bred slackness, and when crisis struck, the realm slid into ruin beyond recovery.

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

translations.literal: Great flourishing followed by decline — such is the fixed principle.
translations.idiomatic: That greatness at its height must give way to decline is the way of things.

sentences.zh: 唐以前以郡領縣而已，元則有路、府、州、縣四等。

translations.literal: Before Tang, commanderies simply governed counties; under the Yuan there were four ranks: circuit, fu, zhou, and county.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Tang, commanderies simply oversaw counties; under the Yuan there were four administrative levels: circuit (lu), prefecture (fu), subprefecture (zhou), and county (xian).

sentences.zh: 大率以路領州、領縣，而腹裏或有以路領府、府領州、州領縣者，其府與州又有不隸路而直隸省者，具載於篇，而其沿革則溯唐而止焉。

translations.literal: Generally circuits governed zhou and counties; in the interior there were also cases of circuits governing fu, fu governing zhou, and zhou governing counties. Some fu and zhou were not subordinate to circuits but reported directly to the Secretariat — all are fully recorded in this chapter, with their histories traced back only as far as Tang.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, circuits oversaw subprefectures and counties; in the metropolitan interior, some circuits also governed prefectures, prefectures governed subprefectures, and subprefectures governed counties. Certain prefectures and subprefectures reported directly to the Secretariat rather than to a circuit. All are recorded in full below, with historical changes traced back only to the Tang dynasty.

translations.literal: This treatise on geography is hereby composed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus is composed the "Treatise on Geography."

translations.literal: All circuits are indented one character below the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: All circuits are set one indent level below the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 府與州直隸省者，亦低於省一字。

translations.literal: Fu and zhou directly subordinate to the Secretariat are also indented one character below the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and subprefectures under direct Secretariat jurisdiction are likewise indented one level below the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其有宣慰司、廉訪司，亦止低於省一字。

translations.literal: Pacification commissions and surveillance commissions are likewise indented only one character below the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissions and surveillance commissions are also indented one level below the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 各路錄事司與路所親領之縣與府、州之隸路者，低於路一字。

translations.literal: Each circuit's record office, counties directly governed by the circuit, and fu and zhou subordinate to the circuit are indented one character below the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit's record office, counties under direct circuit jurisdiction, and prefectures and subprefectures subordinate to the circuit are indented one level below the circuit.

sentences.zh: 府與州所領之縣，低於府與州一字。

translations.literal: Counties governed by fu and zhou are indented one character below the fu and zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Counties under prefectural or subprefectural jurisdiction are indented one level below their parent fu or zhou.

sentences.zh: 府領州、州又領縣者，又低於縣一字。

translations.literal: Where a fu governs a zhou and a zhou in turn governs counties, these are indented one character below the county.
translations.idiomatic: Where a prefecture governs a subprefecture and the subprefecture in turn governs counties, those entries are indented one level below the county.

sentences.zh: 路所親領之縣若府若州，曰領縣若干、府若干、州若干；

translations.literal: Counties, fu, or zhou directly governed by a circuit are listed as "governing X counties, X fu, X zhou";
translations.idiomatic: Counties, prefectures, or subprefectures under direct circuit jurisdiction are listed as "governing X counties, X prefectures, X subprefectures";

sentences.zh: 府與州所領之縣，則曰若干縣，所以別之也。

translations.literal: counties governed by fu and zhou are simply listed as "X counties" — this is to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: counties under fu or zhou jurisdiction are simply listed as "X counties" — a convention to distinguish the two arrangements.

sentences.zh: 中書省統山東西、河北之地，謂之腹裏，為路二十九，州八，屬府三，屬州九十一，屬縣三百四十六。

translations.literal: The central Secretariat governed the lands of Shandong, Shanxi, and Hebei — called the interior — comprising 29 circuits, 8 zhou, 3 subordinate fu, 91 subordinate zhou, and 346 subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: The central Secretariat governed Shandong, Shanxi, and Hebei — the metropolitan interior — comprising twenty-nine circuits, eight subprefectures, three dependent prefectures, ninety-one dependent subprefectures, and three hundred forty-six dependent counties.

sentences.zh: 各路立站，總計一百九十八處。

translations.literal: Relay stations were established on each circuit, totaling 198 locations.
translations.idiomatic: Relay stations were established along each circuit, totaling one hundred ninety-eight locations.

translations.idiomatic: Dadu Circuit — in Tang times, Youzhou, Fanyang Commandery.

translations.idiomatic: The Liao renamed it Yanjing.

translations.literal: Jin moved its capital here and made it Daxing Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin moved its capital here and established Daxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元太祖十年，克燕，初為燕京路，總管大興府。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taizu of Yuan, Yan was taken; it was initially made Yanjing Circuit, administering Daxing Fu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Emperor Taizu, Yan was captured; the city was first made Yanjing Circuit, administering Daxing Prefecture.

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taizong, household registers were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Emperor Taizong, household registers were established.

sentences.zh: 世祖至元元年，中書省臣言：「開平府闕庭所在，加號上都，燕京分立省部，亦乞正名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan under Shizu, Secretariat officials said: "Kaiping Fu is where the imperial court resides; it has been given the additional title Shangdu. Yanjing has been made a separate provincial seat — we also request that its proper name be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhiyuan era, Secretariat officials memorialized: "Kaiping Prefecture, where the imperial court is seated, has been given the additional title Shangdu. Yanjing has been made a separate provincial headquarters — we ask that its proper name also be fixed.

translations.literal: " It was thereupon renamed Zhongdu; Daxing Fu remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: " The city was thereupon renamed Zhongdu, while Daxing Prefecture kept its former designation.

sentences.zh: 四年，始於中都之東北置今城而遷都焉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the present city was first built northeast of Zhongdu and the capital was moved there.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, construction began on the present city northeast of Zhongdu, and the capital was relocated there.

sentences.zh: 京城右擁太行，左挹滄海，枕居庸，奠朔方。

translations.literal: The capital city had the Taihang Mountains on its right and the Bohai Sea on its left; it rested against Juyong Pass and was anchored in the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The capital embraced the Taihang range on the right and the Bohai Sea on the left, rested against Juyong Pass, and stood firm in the northern marches.

sentences.zh: 城方六十里，十一門：正南曰麗正，南之右曰順承，南之左曰文明，北之東曰安貞，北之西曰健德，正東曰崇仁，東之右曰齊化，東之左曰光熙，正西曰和義，西之右曰肅清，西之左曰平則。

translations.literal: The city measured sixty li square, with eleven gates: due south, Lizheng; south-right, Shuncheng; south-left, Wenming; north-east, Anzhen; north-west, Jiande; due east, Chongren; east-right, Qihua; east-left, Guangxi; due west, Heyi; west-right, Suqing; west-left, Pingze.
translations.idiomatic: The city wall measured sixty li on each side, with eleven gates: due south, Lizheng; south-right, Shuncheng; south-left, Wenming; northeast, Anzhen; northwest, Jiande; due east, Chongren; east-right, Qihua; east-left, Guangxi; due west, Heyi; west-right, Suqing; west-left, Pingze.

sentences.zh: 海子在皇城之北、萬壽山之陰，舊名積水潭，聚西北諸泉之水，流入都城而匯于此，汪洋如海，都人因名焉。

translations.literal: The lake lay north of the Imperial City and on the shaded side of Wanshou Mountain; its old name was Jishuitan. It gathered waters from the springs of the northwest, which flowed into the capital and collected here — vast as a sea, whence the people of the capital gave it the name.
translations.idiomatic: The lake lay north of the Imperial City, in the shadow of Longevity Hill. Formerly called Jishuitan, it collected the springs of the northwest, whose waters flowed into the capital and pooled here in an expanse vast as the sea — hence the name the city's people gave it.

sentences.zh: 恣民漁采無禁，擬周之靈沼云。

translations.literal: The people were allowed to fish and gather without restriction, modeled on the Zhou's Spirit Pool.
translations.idiomatic: The people were free to fish and forage without restriction, in the manner of the Zhou dynasty's Spirit Pool.

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year four hundred Han garrison troops at Karakorum were ordered: one hundred were kept on guard and the rest were sent to farm at Hanghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year four hundred Han garrison troops at Karakorum were ordered to remain—one hundred kept on guard while the rest were sent to farm at Hanghai.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，于六衛漢軍內撥一千人赴青海屯田。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen one thousand men were drafted from the Han garrisons of the six guards to farm at Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanzhen one thousand men were drawn from the Han garrisons of the six guards for garrison farming at Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 北方立站帖裏幹、木憐、納憐等一百一十九處。

translations.literal: In the north 119 relay stations were established, including Tieligan, Mulian, Nalian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the north one hundred nineteen relay stations were established, including Tieligan, Mulian, and Nalian.
